candidates.draft_body:
Jubilees (Ethiopian tradition) Book of Jubilees (Mäṣḥafä Kufāle) (c. 150 BC)

'And Rebecca took goodly raiment of her elder son Esau, which was with her in the house, and she clothed Jacob her younger son with them, and put the skins of the kids upon his hands and on the exposed parts of his neck' — Jubilees follows the Gen 27 deception narrative without softening it. Tewahedo Andǝmta exegesis on this passage takes a distinctive position: the deception is NOT condoned but is canonically PERMITTED by divine providence to bring about the predetermined blessing — Isaac's intent to bless Esau was itself contrary to the earlier 'the elder shall serve the younger' (Gen 25:23 = Jub 19:31). The Tewahedo theological reading: God's providence works through human action including human moral ambiguity without destroying free will or sanctioning the deceit per se. (The Tewahedo distinction between divine-permission and divine-command is sharper than the Western Augustinian framing.)
